sources.cite: Crane ChemPharma & Energy, Pacific CSV cast steel valves, installation, operation and maintenance manual CPE-PACIFIC-CSV-IOM-EN-LT (2018): gate valve figure p. 12, operating the handwheel §2.1 p. 13 (the handwheel on the stem nut under the handwheel nut), parts list, disassembly and reassembly p. 14

body.name: Valve body
body.does: Holds the pressure and the flow's way straight through. It stays bolted between its pipe flanges when the valve is opened.

seat_rings.name: Seat rings
seat_rings.does: The two rings the wedge closes against, one each side of it. They stay in the body: the maintenance steps never take them out.

wedge.name: Wedge
wedge.does: The closure member: a wedge whose two faces close on the seat rings. Lifted by the stem clear of the bore, the valve is fully open.
wedge.material: Cast steel, hard-faced at the seat

stem.name: Stem
stem.does: Carries the wedge on its T-head. Its thread runs in the stem nut, so turning the handwheel raises or lowers it; how far it stands out of the yoke shows how far the valve is open.

bonnet.name: Bonnet and yoke
bonnet.does: Closes the body over the wedge on its gasket, carries the packing box round the stem and, in its yoke, the stem nut.

packing.name: Packing, gland and gland flange
packing.does: Rings of graphite packing squeezed round the stem by the gland under the gland flange, so the process cannot leak along the stem.
packing.material: Graphite rings, steel gland and flange

stem_nut.name: Stem nut
stem_nut.does: Turns in the yoke's head, held by its retainer: the handwheel turns it, and its thread drives the stem up or down.

handwheel.name: Handwheel
handwheel.does: Turned by hand to open (anticlockwise) or close the valve; it sits on the stem nut under the handwheel nut.

text: The body stays bolted between its pipe flanges.
why: The bonnet, the stem and the wedge all come out upwards, without disturbing the pipes.

text: The seat rings stay in the body: look at their faces for cuts and wear.
why: Crane's steps never take the seat rings out of the body.
needs: body
The seat rings are in the body.
The body stays on its pipes.

text: Lower the wedge into the body between its seat rings, the way round it was marked when it came out.
why: In the shop the wedge is hung on the stem's T-head and goes in with the bonnet assembly; the steps here fit each part in its place.
needs: seat_rings
The wedge closes on the seat rings: they are there first.
Lift the wedge out before anything is done to the seat rings.

text: Put the stem's T-head down into the wedge's slot.
needs: wedge
The stem carries the wedge: put the wedge in first.
Draw the stem up out of the wedge before the wedge comes out.

text: Fit a new bonnet gasket and lower the bonnet over the stem onto the body.
why: Crane lifts the bonnet off with the stem and the wedge on it, then takes the wedge off the stem and draws the stem out by turning the handwheel.
needs: stem
The bonnet goes on over the stem: put the stem in first.
Lift the bonnet off before the stem comes out.

text: Fit the bonnet studs and nuts and tighten them evenly, crosswise.
needs: bonnet
The nuts hold the bonnet down: set it on first.
Take the bonnet nuts off before the bonnet is lifted.

text: Screw the stem nut onto the stem's thread in the yoke's head and fit its retainer.
why: Crane takes the stem nut out last, and only when it needs renewing: its retainer's set screws or tack welds come off first.
needs: bonnet
The stem nut turns in the yoke's head: set the bonnet on first.
Take the stem nut out before the bonnet comes off.
stem
The stem's thread runs in the stem nut: put the stem in first.
Take the stem nut off before the stem comes out.

text: Put the handwheel on the stem nut and screw the handwheel nut down on it.
needs: stem_nut
The handwheel sits on the stem nut: fit it first.
Take the handwheel off before the stem nut.

text: Put new packing rings over the stem into the packing box, then the gland and the gland flange, and tighten the gland's eyebolt nuts evenly.
why: Taking apart, Crane loosens the gland's nuts first, then the bonnet's, and hooks the old packing out once the bonnet is on the bench.
needs: bonnet_bolts
Pack the stem when the bonnet is bolted down.
Take the gland off and the packing out before the bonnet nuts.
